records.summary: Rope Work involves tying secure knots, crafting rope-based tools, and setting up climbing or sailing equipment. Itʼs useful for setting traps, climbing, and securing gear. DC 10: Tying basic knots, securing a simple load, tying up an unresisting person. DC 15: Tying a secure climbing knot, making a strong lasso, fastening a heavy load. DC 20: Tying complex sailing knots, creating a reliable safety harness, securing a person attempting to escape. DC 25: Crafting intricate rope structures, improvising a reliable rope bridge, securing a load under extreme conditions.

Sigilcrafting involves creating magical symbols, wards, and charms that carry specific effects. Itʼs useful for imbuing objects, creating barriers, or invoking magical protection. DC 10: Drawing a simple protective sigil, creating a minor charm, marking a basic rune. DC 15: Crafting a sigil to ward off small creatures, inscribing a rune for minor luck, creating a basic enchantment. DC 20: Creating a potent ward for specific creatures, imbuing an item with moderate magic, crafting a defensive rune. DC 25: Crafting a sigil with strong magical properties, creating an advanced ward against magic, inscribing a powerful artifact with protective runes.

Purpose: Skill checks are rolled whenever a character attempts an action with a chance of failure, such as climbing a cliff, deceiving a guard, or interpreting ancient texts. Mechanics: To perform a skill check, roll a D20 and add relevant modifiers from skills, attributes, or other bonuses. If the total equals or exceeds the Difficulty Class (DC) set by the GM, the action succeeds; otherwise, it fails.

Sleight of Hand covers picking pockets, concealing items, and performing quick, subtle movements. This skill is crucial for rogues, magicians, and characters who rely on stealthy tricks. DC 10: Palming a small item, performing a basic coin trick, hiding an object in plain sight. DC 15: Lifting a purse in a crowd, switching objects unnoticed, performing a minor magic trick. DC 20: Picking a pocket without detection, concealing a weapon during a search, planting an item on someone unnoticed. DC 25: Performing a complex magic trick, pickpocketing under close observation, swapping objects without anyone noticing.

Specialized Driving Proficiency covers handling more complex vehicles, from trucks to heavy machinery. This skill is essential for advanced driving in challenging environments. DC 10: Maneuvering basic off-road terrain, parking a large vehicle, driving a utility truck. DC 15: Navigating rough terrain, parking heavy equipment, driving under moderate stress. DC 20: Driving specialized vehicles in tough terrain, handling obstacles, operating utility vehicles under pressure. DC 25: Performing evasive maneuvers in rugged terrain, handling emergency situations, driving at high speeds off-road.

Street Smarts covers practical knowledge of urban environments, identifying threats, recognizing scams, and navigating safely in dangerous areas. Itʼs key for city-based characters. DC 10: Identifying local hangouts, spotting low-level scams, recognizing common street signs and symbols. DC 15: Finding a safe route in a risky area, recognizing the signs of a con, identifying local gang affiliations. DC 20: Gathering information discreetly, avoiding dangerous spots at night, detecting hidden criminal activities. DC 25: Navigating hostile gang territories, blending in seamlessly with locals, finding shelter in a foreign underworld.

Survival aids in living off the land, finding food and water, building shelters, and enduring extreme conditions. Itʼs ideal for characters exploring wilderness areas or facing harsh environments. DC 10: Identifying edible plants, finding clean water nearby, recognizing safe camping spots. DC 15: Tracking a common animal, setting up a basic shelter, navigating in familiar wilderness. DC 20: Tracking a cautious animal over difficult terrain, making fire in damp conditions, finding rare food sources. DC 25: Surviving in extreme weather, finding water in a desert, tracking a creature across harsh terrain.

Swimming measures your ability to move and maneuver in water. Itʼs essential for crossing bodies of water, rescuing others, or surviving in aquatic encounters. DC 10: Swimming across calm water, keeping afloat in still water, wading through a shallow stream. DC 15: Swimming across a gentle current, staying afloat while lightly burdened, navigating underwater briefly. DC 20: Swimming against a strong current, holding breath underwater for a long time, carrying someone while swimming. DC 25: Swimming in a stormy sea, maneuvering underwater for extended periods, towing multiple people through rough water.

Tracking lets you follow trails left by creatures or people, identifying signs of passage, and understanding environmental clues. Itʼs key for hunters, scouts, and investigators. DC 10: Following a well-defined trail, identifying recent footprints, tracking a common animal. DC 15: Tracking an animal through dense forest, following faint footprints, identifying various animal signs. DC 20: Tracking through light rain or snow, following a trail thatʼs a day old, identifying a single creature in a mixed group. DC 25: Tracking through heavy rain, following a week-old trail, identifying rare species by traces alone.

Tumble allows you to perform acrobatic rolls, flips, and evasive maneuvers, often used in combat to dodge attacks or position yourself advantageously. DC 10: Performing a simple roll to reduce fall impact, dodging a low obstacle, rolling forward in combat. DC 15: Tumbling over an opponent, flipping to avoid an attack, dodging quickly to avoid a trap. DC 20: Tumbling between multiple opponents, performing a mid-air flip, diving safely from a significant height. DC 25: Performing a complex series of tumbles in combat, rolling through dangerous terrain, evading multiple attackers at once.

Zero-G Maneuvers covers movement and control in zero-gravity environments. Itʼs useful for characters in space settings, aiding in navigation, combat, and handling weightlessness. DC 10: Moving in zero-G without spinning, using small bursts for movement, keeping balanced. DC 15: Changing direction smoothly, grabbing onto handholds, moving with precision. DC 20: Performing controlled flips, maneuvering quickly across open space, balancing while adjusting gear. DC 25: Evading obstacles mid-flight, docking onto moving objects, maneuvering through tight zero-G spaces.
•Effect: You gain advantage on saving throws against diseases and poisons. Additionally, you recover from exhaustion twice as quickly when resting.
•Effect: When subjected to form-changing magic or effects, you can reduce the duration of the effect to a single round and gain advantage on the saving throw against it.

Effect: Once per long rest, when failing a Persuasion, Deception, or Negotiation check, you may reroll with advantage by adjusting your approach mid-conversation. This reflects human social adaptability and persistence.

•Effect: Once per long rest, you can activate your tattoos to create a burst of vibrant, magical graffiti in a 10-foot radius. Enemies in the area must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or be blinded until the end of their next turn. Allies in the area gain advantage on their next attack roll.

records.summary: Advanced Fertilizer -2 to Growth DC, +25% yield
Farms inside starships, stations, or magical bastions must use enclosed methods like hydroponics or arcane terraria.
To begin farming within a base, a Farming Zone must be constructed. Once in place, you may assign plots (acres) to different crops.
Each Foraging Zone can be assigned a character or staff each Base Turn to gather resources. Alternatively, automated systems (drones, caretakers, or golems) can be used if installed.
Each acre advances through 3 stages: Early, Mid, and Mature. Each Base Turn, make a Growth Check (Survival or Nature) per acre. Plant Acre Begin a new cropʼs cycle on prepared land.
checks, apply fertilizers, defend against hazards. Harvest Acre Gather the full yield if mature. Rest Acre Skip farming actions this turn to recover land quality (+1 Health).

•Offspring inherit 1 temperament at random from each parent. •With selective breeding (Animal Handling DC 15+), you may choose one temperament the offspring inherits. •Some temperaments are dominant (Docile, Aggressive, Territorial), while others are recessive (Aloof, Loyal, Nervous), affecting likelihood of inheritance.
Artistic activities include painting, sculpture, music, writing, or other creative expression, allowing characters to express themselves and even earn reputation or income.
Spending time with family or friends helps strengthen relationships and provides emotional support, benefiting morale and mental resilience.
Characters need time to relax and recharge through hobbies, games, or social activities, helping them reduce stress and increase morale.
Each facility may perform one of the following orders per Base Turn if active and maintained:
•Size: 250 sq ft •Actions: Gain inner clarity •Upkeep: None if used by owner •Mechanics: Advantage on next save or insight check

Parties may choose to build interconnected bases that dock or travel together. This opens gameplay like: •Specialized nodes: one crafting pod, one military pod, one arcane lab •Base caravans or flying flotillas •Trade convoys that travel between realms •Combine base defense bonuses when connected Each player maintains autonomy but may share: •Power pool (if synced)

•Most upgrades take 1–3 Base Turns to complete. •You may complete 1 upgrade per Base Turn, or 2 if you have a construction team or magic. •Some upgrades may be limited by your current base size (e.g., teleport pads require Large+). •GMs can create world-specific constraints such as resource bottlenecks, zoning laws, or permission from factions.

•The party is traveling for several days •The group is resting or recovering at their base •Time is skipped between adventures •Players assign orders or workers to base tasks 📌 You can choose between weekly and monthly Base Turns depending on the gameʼs pacing. For fast-paced campaigns, use weekly turns. For domain-level play, use monthly turns.

If the business is staffed, each employee may contribute to quality (or cause problems). Each day (or week), employees roll a skill check based on their role:

If a player-character is present during downtime, they may take on key tasks. Once per week, a character may choose one: 3H. Multiversal Factors In Multiversal, unusual factors may affect business outcomes: •Dimensional Flux: If near a reality breach, roll with disadvantage •Local Holidays: Can boost or reduce traffic (GM discretion) •Empire Activity: Tax checks, bureaucratic shutdowns, or bribes may affect weeks GMs may incorporate Multiversal Events (see Section 7) to keep business play dynamic and narratively integrated.

Each day or week (depending on how the business is run), employees roll a skill check related to their job: •Success (Meet DC): Normal income and reputation gain. •Enhanced Success (Beat DC by 5+): +10% income for the day/week, or +1 Reputation. •Failure: -10% income and risk of negative event (see Section 7A).

Morale determines how loyal and productive employees are. Each week, roll a Charisma (DC 10) morale check: •Failure: One employee loses morale (−1 to checks) or threatens to quit. •Success: No effect. •Enhanced Success: All staff gain +1 to checks next week.

•Inventory: Food, synthdrinks, neuromods •Service: Entertainment, hacking booths •Production: Drug kitchen or nootropic forge Track each category independently or roll once weekly for all combined operations at a +2 DC. 5F. Inventory Hazards & Spoilage (Optional Rule) Some goods may decay, warp, or attract attention: •Biological Spoilage: Requires proper storage or preservation. •Magical Drift: May require containment glyphs or stabilizers. •Blacklisted Materials: May trigger inspections or theft attempts. Track these using a Decay Table or make weekly checks to avoid loss or consequences.
